slides.title:
Every environment
we inherit has one device
*nobody can log into*.
slides.body:
It is never the
least important one.

slides.title: It's the core switch
slides.body:
In the oldest building.
Or the firewall in front of what
finance uses on the *31st*.

slides.title: And it works
slides.body:
Six years forwarding traffic
without a complaint — which is
*exactly* why nobody opened it.

slides.title: This isn't about passwords
slides.body:
It is the point where operational
ownership *stopped transferring*.

slides.title: Credentials are the symptom
slides.body:
The part you can see
from outside.

slides.title: Underneath it, the same gap
steps: The change history nobody can reconstruct.
The config that was never backed up.

slides.title: So "get into the device"
slides.body:
Is the wrong goal.
It's a ticket, *not a fix*.

slides.title: The real work
steps: Find every device whose last change predates the team.
Name an owner. Put it on the leaver's checklist.

slides.title: It isn't your risk.
slides.body:
It's the only one that
*raised its hand*.

Follow *@mzsnetworks*
